title: Delete tze_hud_resource sharing, GC, refcount, budget and font-cache layer
description:
Goal: Delete the unreachable resource layer; keep only what other crates call.

Non-goals: Changing upload, ResidentLedger, RuntimeWidgetStore or wire codes.

Governing spec: docs/scope.md T8 row (delete code without a current user; behavior tests tied to docs/invariants.md; resource tests; llvmpipe recipe; strip pre-reset refs) and 'Working rules' (prefer deleting over generalizing; tests guard behavior a user would notice, not internal structure); docs/vision.md; docs/invariants.md; CLAUDE.md Rules; AGENTS.md (just recipes).

T7 boundary: do not edit crates/tze_hud_projection/**, crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/portal_projection_driver.rs, crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/windowed/portal.rs, crates/tze_hud_input/src/{composer_draft,portal_resize}.rs, crates/tze_hud_config/src/portal_tokens.rs, crates/tze_hud_mcp/src/portal_op.rs or tests/integration/text_stream_portal_*.rs; keep every pub item those files import until T7 (epic hud-lirh2) lands.

Line refs are at windows-release-pipeline@44d355ef (same content as main@1eb8f7cb); re-grep symbols before editing. The planning survey is not persisted; this bead is self-contained.
design:
Files:
- crates/tze_hud_resource/src/{budget.rs 493, sharing.rs 658, gc.rs 653, refcount.rs 426, store.rs 433, font_cache.rs 475}
- lib.rs:57-103 re-exports; validation.rs:481-540 (`validate_upload`, re-implemented by upload.rs); unused consts types.rs:158-195

Evidence:
Every pub item in the six files has 0 references outside the crate and they reference only each other. External callers use only ResourceStore::{new,new_with_resident_ledger,handle_upload_*,abort_all_uploads,font_bytes} (protocol session_server/upload.rs:262,365; mod.rs:571; runtime font_loader.rs:143), RuntimeWidgetStore (protocol widgets.rs:406), ResidentLedger, ResourceId. Narrow-to-pub(crate) rustc run agrees.

Approach:
Delete the six modules and their re-exports; if ResourceStore lives in store.rs, keep the struct and only the methods named above. Narrow remaining pub items to what other crates use.

Tests:
Delete the 61 inline tests in those modules. Keep upload, runtime_widget_store, resident_ledger, validation and types tests incl. `wire_codes_are_stable` (types.rs:415).

Expected delta: about -3,250

Every test named in docs/invariants.md is kept, or moved/renamed with docs/invariants.md updated in the same PR. Local builds on this host need `PROTOC=$HOME/.local/protoc/bin/protoc` (/usr/bin/protoc 3.12 fails on types.proto).
acceptance_criteria:
1. `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean.
2. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
3. `cargo test -p tze_hud_resource -p tze_hud_protocol -p tze_hud_runtime` passes (quiet).
4. Deletion check: `git grep -nE 'font_cache|refcount::|sharing::|gc::|budget::' -- crates/tze_hud_resource` prints nothing (no remaining references).
5. Every test named in docs/invariants.md still exists (grep each name) or docs/invariants.md was updated in the same PR.
6. `just ci` is green once before handoff.

title: Give every gRPC session rejection an actionable hint
description:
Outcome: every existing gRPC session rejection envelope has a stable unchanged code and a nonempty hint naming the client’s next valid action. Seven construction sites currently set an empty hint: crates/tze_hud_protocol/src/auth.rs:162; src/session_server/handshake.rs:141,338; src/session_server/mod.rs:221,235,282,770. The model cannot recover reliably from these failures although docs/invariants.md:132–136 requires an actionable hint on every rejection. Fix the full pre-existing surface, not only one happy example. Maintenance authority: current docs/invariants.md §§8–9 and docs/scope.md T8 / Working rules, with docs/vision.md Trust model. This repairs an existing contract; it does not change the owner-selected authentication posture, permissions, API, or invariant semantics. Pre-reset RFC/OpenSpec/doctrine are history, not authority. Audit base: 17de3331b11a1ee55fa22197fd13b99b26dac267. Evidence: test_results/reconciliation/hud-bstmy.2.6/report.md, follow-ups.json and source inventories, in evidence PR #1354 (https://github.com/tzeusy-org/tze-hud/pull/1354). Re-grep current main before implementation; cited lines are the audit baseline.

Non-goals: changing accepted credentials, LocalSocketCredential loopback evaluation, AgentDirectory identity/allow rules, PSK pairing/storage, wire codes/messages, protocol version rules, lease/token/budget outcomes, transactional delivery or close ordering, successful replies, transport Status semantics, or replacing the owner’s trust model. Do not remove legacy helpers here; that is hud-bstmy.2.8. Do not expose PSKs, resume tokens, credential text, or identity-enumeration details in hints.
design:
Owned surface / trust map: auth::identify_session evaluates an incoming credential and turns failure into AuthRejection; handshake::send_auth_failed forwards that to SessionError. Init and Resume separately call runtime MutationBudgetEnforcer::register_session and forward its Reject code/message. The session loop sends SessionError when initial inbound read closes/errors, first payload is wrong, or sequence validation fails. These are the same existing client/server boundary; change only recovery text. AgentDirectory and auth::evaluate_auth_credential remain authorities for admission. Runtime BudgetEnforcer remains authority for budget admission. Generated proto SessionError already contains code/message/hint: no schema, generated-stub, persisted-state, config or migration change.

Sweep: inspect all production SessionError and AuthRejection constructors, RequestResult failure helpers and the resource error envelope; distinguish successful inline test fixtures from rejected responses. Baseline empty-hint inventory above is the minimum, not a future-proof scan root. Preserve existing stable codes including dynamic enforcer codes; do not force SessionError codes into the separate RequestResult closed set. The existing grpc_codes_are_in_the_shared_set scanner reads only verbs.rs/mutations.rs and is not a hint gate.

Behavior matrix: valid Init/Resume, accepted local credentials and successful requests retain their bytes/outcomes apart from unrelated timestamps. Failed local/non-PSK credentials get a generic instruction to use the paired credential, without disclosing a secret or changing acceptance. Init/Resume budget refusals retain rejection and current cleanup/token behavior and give an action compatible with the failure; do not promise reuse of a consumed resume token. Closed/error initial reads direct a fresh SessionInit; wrong first payload names Init/Resume; sequence failures direct a fresh stream with monotonic sequencing. Concurrent rejected clients get the same deterministic category hint with no shared mutable hint state or new locks/awaits. Retry/replay preserves all current semantics: ClaimTile/Hold/Clear caches stay untouched, resume tokens remain single-use, terminal session errors still terminate at the same point. No persistence/deferred migration exists; errors are transient envelopes. Rollback is a normal revert of the hint/test diff and restores prior behavior without data conversion.

Cohesion / sequencing: E and hud-bstmy.2.8 share auth.rs and protocol fixtures; serialize E before P. Separate rollback/review is justified because E is a P1 externally visible affordance repair, whereas P removes dead production interfaces. One primary owner; no parallel edits to auth/handshake.

Docs impact: no semantic change to docs/invariants.md or docs/api.md and no new docs file. If error guidance is documented, make a concise same-PR clarification in docs/api.md Errors while preserving codes and identity rules; otherwise explain none in the PR because the existing contract already requires this behavior. Gate species: behavior-executing error-envelope tests only. No added hint grep/snapshot/property suite or duplicate case. Nearest existing gates: session_server/tests/session_handshake.rs test_handle_session_init_local_socket_non_loopback_auth_failed, test_handle_session_resume_local_socket_non_loopback_auth_failed, test_sequence_gap_exceeded, test_sequence_regression. Extend their assertions. Add one table for uncovered Init/Resume register_session refusal via a rejecting existing enforcer fixture, and one table for uncovered initial-read close/error/wrong-payload branches, driving the real handler/loop decision seam (not synthesizing a SessionError literal). Expected Tests: +2 ~4 -0. Existing bogus-token and version-error hint gates are reused without a second species.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Read the current seven sites and enumerate every production SessionError/AuthRejection constructor plus RequestResult/resource failure envelopes. Every previously empty rejection hint is replaced by actionable next-step text; code, message meaning, rejection/close order and auth/permission outcome stay unchanged.
2. Extend the four named existing local-credential/sequence behavior tests to assert a nonempty category-appropriate hint, retaining their rejection assertions. They must execute the original handler/loop seam rather than inspect source or a constructed error literal.
3. Add exactly the two planned behavior tables for the previously ungated register_session Init/Resume failures and initial-read close/error/wrong-payload categories. Use actual handlers and existing fixtures; assertion coverage must include the emitted code and hint. Do not add a parallel structural hint guard.
4. Valid handshake/resume, wrong PSK, accepted loopback behavior, single-use/wrong-agent resume tokens, unchanged sequence closure and existing ClaimTile/Hold/Clear replay remain pinned by the current tests. No new auth grant, fallback, token policy or error code is introduced; hints contain no credential/resume secret or new identity disclosure.
5. Preserve concurrent-session isolation and transactional ordering by avoiding new shared mutable state, locks, waits or sends. The same rejection category produces deterministic guidance; retransmitted operations retain existing cached outcomes.
6. Run focused protocol handshake/resume/sequence tests, cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --workspace, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings. Use CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 on this constrained host; no all-features build. Follow repository full local gate policy before implementation handoff and record Tests: +2 ~4 -0 (justify any deviation before broadening).
7. Record docs impact explicitly: existing invariant/API semantics are preserved; only an accurate same-PR guidance clarification is allowed. PR describes seven-path coverage, tests and untouched admission authority. Reconcile the current named invariant-test inventory and report any additional unresolved envelope gap rather than changing trust posture.

title: Remove sleep polling from gRPC disconnect invariant tests
description:
Outcome: the three named gRPC disconnect/resume/grace invariant tests observe actual asynchronous session cleanup without wall-clock sleep polling, then advance grace only through TestClock. protocol/src/session_server/tests/invariants.rs:54/67 currently uses Instant::now and 5ms sleeps in wait_for_lease_state; all three tests call connect_hold_tile_and_disconnect through that helper. The lease semantics pass today, but this waiting instrument violates docs/invariants.md:144–149 (time tests use injected clocks and no sleeps). Maintenance authority: that current invariant contract and docs/scope.md T8 Working rules; repair the test instrument without changing production behavior. Evidence: test_results/reconciliation/hud-bstmy.2.6/report.md, follow-ups.json, source/test inventories and dead-code-*.log, in PR #1354 https://github.com/tzeusy-org/tze-hud/pull/1354. Cited lines are baseline 17de3331b11a1ee55fa22197fd13b99b26dac267; re-grep current main before acting.

Non-goals: implementing a different lease/grace/resume state machine, directly forcing lease state in a test, bypassing actual transport drop, adding a production clock/event architecture, changing cleanup/token/enforcer ordering, new wall-time semantic deadlines, new scenario tests, or a parallel structural no-sleep guard. Protected T7 caller surface: crates/tze_hud_projection/**; crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/portal_projection_driver.rs and src/windowed/portal.rs; crates/tze_hud_input/src/{composer_draft,portal_resize}.rs; crates/tze_hud_config/src/portal_tokens.rs; crates/tze_hud_mcp/src/portal_op.rs; tests/integration/text_stream_portal_*.rs. Do not edit these files or remove public symbols used by those real production paths until hud-lirh2 lands. The five scene-portal-to-proto converters at protocol/convert.rs:1029,1073,1121,1160,1232 remain excluded.
design:
Surface/trust map: own protocol/src/session_server/tests/invariants.rs wait_for_lease_state/connect_hold_tile_and_disconnect and the three existing test bodies. Observe the real session_server/mod.rs:521+ cleanup boundary: session removal, guard disarm, SceneGraph injected now_millis, disconnect of active owned leases, resume-token insertion at the same injected time, abort_all_uploads and enforcer session removal. Use an existing awaitable completion/event observation if it exposes this boundary; if absent, add only the narrow established test-only cleanup witness keyed by session/namespace. Register it before dropping the actual stream/handle, so a fast cleanup cannot lose a wakeup. The witness observes completion and must not cause cleanup, mutate lease state, consume tokens or expose secrets. It must not signal another concurrent session or create a production default-feature API. Hold no scene/session lock while awaiting it.

Behavior matrix: real transport drop completes existing cleanup and produces the same orphaned leases/tile badge; resume within TestClock grace restores the same IDs/state; expiry at the existing injected-clock boundary rejects resume and reclaims resources. Concurrent sessions have isolated observations; repeated observation/drop uses existing transport semantics and cannot double-remove sessions or manufacture a cleanup. Replayed lease operations and single-use/agent-bound tokens retain existing behavior. TestClock alone advances semantic grace; an existing bounded watchdog may protect a stuck harness, but wall time/sleep may not determine state correctness or advance grace. Failure means a clear awaited-cleanup failure, not polling until a coincidental state appears. No wire/persisted schema changes; rollback removes only test instrument changes.

Docs impact: no contract/API semantic update; adjust the helper comment only if it describes polling, and record compliance with docs/invariants.md §§9–10. Nearest gate species is the existing behavior tests only: grpc_disconnect_orphans_leases_and_badges_tiles, grpc_resume_within_grace_restores_same_lease_and_tile, grpc_grace_expiry_reclaims_orphaned_lease_and_rejects_resume. Extend these three and no others (Tests: +0 ~3 -0); do not add a source regex guard or duplicate timing table. Run focused protocol tests, relevant invariant inventory and repository formatting/workspace gates with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1. Include tests/integration for any helper type/feature change. Cohesion/serialization: depend on hud-bstmy.2.8 because P narrows the same invariant fixture constructors; run after E/P and keep actual cleanup authority unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Replace wait_for_lease_state Instant deadline and sleep polling with an awaitable observation of completed real session cleanup. Prefer the existing completion/event mechanism; any necessary witness is narrow, test-only, keyed to the real session and registered before transport drop. The test must still drop the actual stream and await the runtime cleanup, not directly set lease state.
2. Extend the three existing grpc_disconnect_orphans_leases_and_badges_tiles, grpc_resume_within_grace_restores_same_lease_and_tile and grpc_grace_expiry_reclaims_orphaned_lease_and_rejects_resume gates to use this observation. Retain assertions on orphan badges, original lease/tile IDs, resume validity, expiry/reclamation and actual cleanup effects. TestClock exclusively drives grace correctness; no sleeps or wall-clock polling in these semantic paths.
3. The observation cannot lose fast completion, cross-signal concurrent sessions, hold shared locks across await, alter cleanup ordering, consume tokens or produce cleanup itself. Existing resume/replay/idempotence and agent-bound/single-use token tests pass; no auth, lease, resource, error-code, wire or persisted-format behavior changes.
4. Run the three focused gates and relevant existing protocol token/lifecycle invariants, cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1; use applicable repository local gates. Reconcile the current named test inventory and report Tests: +0 ~3 -0, with no new duplicate or structural test species.
5. Record that docs/invariants.md now matches the real helper and no API or semantic docs change is needed; update an inaccurate helper comment only. Show the before/after instrument and real cleanup observation seam in the PR.

title: Reconcile T8.1a against main after all coverage repairs
description:
Outcome: after all five gen-1 gap repairs and evidence PR #1354 are merged to main, produce a fresh read-only gen-2 spec-to-code reconciliation of T8.1a for parent hud-bstmy.2. Report every negative/universal requirement and every guard instrument with file:line evidence classed implemented, partial, missing or deviates; issue closure is based on verified main behavior, not old evidence or deleted names. Gen-1 hud-bstmy.2.6 found residual dead resource/protocol/scene islands, empty session error hints and real-time invariant polling. Concrete repairs are R=hud-bstmy.2.7, P=hud-bstmy.2.8, S=hud-bstmy.2.9, E=hud-bstmy.2.10 and T=hud-bstmy.2.11. Maintenance authority: docs/scope.md:37 (T8 delete code without a current user), :62–65 (prefer deletion and behavior tests while preserving invariants), docs/vision.md:85–99 and :107 (delete deferred islands; no future-facing frameworks), and the current docs/invariants.md. Pre-reset RFC/OpenSpec/doctrine are history, not authority. Read each original sibling requirement (.2.1–.2.5), these five repaired packets/PRs, and the parent acceptance directly. Cited lines are baseline 17de3331b11a1ee55fa22197fd13b99b26dac267; re-grep current main before acting.

Non-goals: implementation/test/code edits, changing owner trust/auth posture or specs to match gaps, inventing missing production callers from tests/comments/name collisions, new guard species, duplicating separately owned pre-reset cleanup hud-bstmy.8.3, or closing issues yourself. This is the single terminal gen-2 reconciliation for this parent; do not create parallel subsystem recon beads. If gaps remain, return dedupe-ready exact gap candidates and a proposed gen-3 follow-up for coordinator; gen-3 is the ceiling and gen-4 is forbidden. Protected T7 caller surface: crates/tze_hud_projection/**; crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/portal_projection_driver.rs and src/windowed/portal.rs; crates/tze_hud_input/src/{composer_draft,portal_resize}.rs; crates/tze_hud_config/src/portal_tokens.rs; crates/tze_hud_mcp/src/portal_op.rs; tests/integration/text_stream_portal_*.rs. Do not edit these files or remove public symbols used by those real production paths until hud-lirh2 lands. The five scene-portal-to-proto converters at protocol/convert.rs:1029,1073,1121,1160,1232 remain excluded.
design:
Surface/trust map: read all current resource/protocol/scene production and test surfaces owned by original children hud-bstmy.2.1–.2.5 and new repairs hud-bstmy.2.7–.2.11, plus all actual callers in app/crates/examples/tests. Confirm the live boundary chain (AgentDirectory and Init/Resume identification, capability admission, mutation/upload conversion, SceneGraph/lease/policy authority, ResourceStore/ResidentLedger/RuntimeWidgetStore, runtime consumers) and separate production from test/dev and deferred T7 callers. Audit scene-side policy, pure policy evaluators and direct runtime enforcement when classifying retained items; do not mistake their ownership. Verify protobuf TimingHints versus deleted scene TimingHints by actual type, and every grouped reexport/cfg path. Include wire/session envelopes and the actual disconnect cleanup time source. No production data or secrets may enter evidence.

Audit matrix: verify normal handshake/upload/mutation lifecycle and named invariants, all rejection hints and stable code categories, concurrent session/resource isolation and actual completion observation, resume/replay/idempotence and cleanup/reclamation, current defaults/serialization compatibility and protected T7 behavior. Read real handlers/call sites and nearest existing gates; test presence or success does not prove universal coverage. Re-enumerate every production rejection constructor/path and every pre-existing deletion obligation. Evaluate each instrument for source roots, regex limits, name/cfg ambiguity, timeout/clock provenance, and blind spots: advisory scripts/dead_code.py does not include app, counts inline tests/comments, conflates unrelated names, and retains grouped reexports; its exit only establishes compiler completion. No newly invented parallel test suite.

Sequencing/readiness: suggested blocking dependencies are the five concrete repair IDs only. Original .2.1–.2.5 are already closed antecedents but their merge/main reachability still requires verification. External prerequisite is PR #1354 state MERGED with merged commit/evidence reachable on main; do not depend on hud-bstmy.2.6 closure, and do not create a .2.6/GEN2 cycle. Before recon, confirm every repair PR is merged and the current fetched main contains each outcome; closed status alone is insufficient. Use a fresh isolated audit head and record its SHA, tool versions and exact commands. Rollback is removal of a report-only artifact; no runtime migration/state change.

Docs impact: production/spec/API docs are read-only; create only the durable gen-2 report/evidence under test_results/reconciliation/hud-bstmy.2.12/ (selectively force-add allowed by AGENTS), with valid Discovered-Follow-Ups-JSON and Blockers-JSON arrays. Commit/push an evidence-only PR and coordinator confirms its main landing before terminal closure; a nonempty gap set keeps the recon blocked awaiting materialized repairs and, if needed, one gen-3 terminal follow-up. Do not close it yourself. Tests: +0 ~0 -0. Re-run exact four sibling deletion inventories, full current named-invariant definition inventory, actual narrowed lib scans and affected existing behavior gates from a recorded current main head; no new code/tests. CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 and repository just/llvmpipe recipes constrain execution. Cohesion override: one cross-child recon is intentionally broader than one subsystem because the terminal requirement is to detect seams, universal path gaps and weak instruments across all five repairs; separate subsystem recon would duplicate gates and miss ownership crossings.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Before auditing, verify PR #1354 is MERGED and its evidence is reachable on main; verify hud-bstmy.2.7/.2.8/.2.9/.2.10/.2.11 outcomes and original .2.1–.2.5 merged outcomes are present on the recorded fetched main SHA. No dependency on .2.6 closure and no self/cyclic deps. If an external prerequisite is absent, report its exact blocker and do not claim repaired-state reconciliation.
2. Read parent/all sibling requirements against current docs/scope.md T8/Working rules, docs/invariants.md and docs/vision.md. Produce a complete file:line coverage checklist with implemented/partial/missing/deviates classifications. Sweep every negative/universal requirement across pre-existing production and tests, including resource validation/refcount, protocol helpers/exports, scene timing/helpers, every rejection envelope/hint and no-sleep invariant instrument. Explicitly preserve protected T7 callers/type distinctions.
3. Repeat the four exact deletion checks and named-invariant inventory (72 names at baseline; validate the current complete set exactly once each), current symbol/caller inventories and actual narrowed resource/protocol/scene lib scans. Audit all scanner roots/cfg/name/reexport blind spots and guard coverage; distinguish compile success from no dead code and test existence from behavior execution. Report each retained diagnostic with a real production caller or necessary named test fixture.
4. Run affected existing resource/protocol/scene behavior gates at the real seams: eight store_behavior rejection/admission gates; identity/token/fuzz/replay and E hint gates; live timing/TTL/policy and all three T disconnect/resume/grace gates. Verify failure/concurrency/idempotence/retry/compatibility and time-source authority from current code plus results. No new source-scan/property/snapshot/mirror suite. Record exact commands, SHA, versions, outputs and Tests: +0 ~0 -0, using CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 and applicable repository gates.
5. Persist report and bounded evidence in test_results/reconciliation/hud-bstmy.2.12/, with exact spec/source/test links and valid Discovered-Follow-Ups-JSON/Blockers-JSON arrays. Each gap candidate carries observed behavior, named nearest gate and exact proposed test delta plus a dedupe key; cross-check active/closed repairs before proposing work. Return a proposed gen-3 only if gaps remain, blocked behind concrete materialized gap IDs and evidence merge, never a future self-dependency or gen-4.
6. Keep production/spec/test sources read-only, commit/push the evidence-only outcome and open a reviewable report PR. Coordinator alone applies tracker changes and closes after main merge confirmation and a clean gap set; unresolved gaps remain blocked with branch-pushed recovery. Report documentation impact as evidence-only and preserve current auth/trust/schema semantics.

title: Reconcile spec-to-code (gen-1) for T8.1a: Dead code in protocol, resource and scene
description:
Deep-dive review: compare the original spec/requirements (see epic description and docs/scope.md T8 row, docs/invariants.md) against the implementation delivered by sibling beads under this epic.

Mindset: audit the CODEBASE against the spec, not the sibling diffs against their bead descriptions. Your job is to FALSIFY the coverage claim, not to collect confirming evidence. A requirement counts as implemented only after you have read the implementing code; a test existing or the suite being green is never sufficient evidence by itself.

Workflow:
1. Re-read the epic description and all sibling bead descriptions/acceptance criteria.
2. Audit the code. Start from the sibling diffs, but treat the whole codebase as in scope; spec invariants bind pre-existing code too.
3. For every universal or negative requirement ("no X anywhere", "every Y must", "the only path is Z"): enumerate ALL code paths performing that operation (search the repo) and verify each one.
4. Audit the instruments: for every guardrail/scan test, read its regex, glob and scan roots and check they cover the mandated surface. For every spec scenario confirm ONE gate pins it (a behavior-executing test, or the designated scan guard for structural invariants).
5. Where several surfaces implement the same contract, diff them against each other (filters, defaults, ordering, authz).
6. Produce a checklist mapping every requirement to its implementing bead and code evidence (file:line), classified implemented/partial/missing/deviates.
7. For every partial or missing requirement, report a cold-start-ready gap candidate in Discovered-Follow-Ups-JSON (priority, parent, deps, exact spec link, acceptance evidence, gate species, expected net test delta).
8. When gaps remain, report the need for a gen-2 reconciliation and return blocked-awaiting-coordinator with "coverage gaps remain" as the unblock condition.
9. The coordinator dedupes/materializes gaps and closes lifecycle state; this worker never mutates Beads lifecycle.
design: Spec sources: docs/scope.md T8 row and Working rules, docs/invariants.md (every named test exists), docs/vision.md, plus every sibling bead under hud-bstmy.2 (their Files/Evidence lists define the deletion surface; verify each deletion grep is empty and each kept test exists). Runs last among implementation siblings. Escalation (needs-human) siblings are deliberately NOT dependencies: their default is status quo, so reconciliation must not wait on an owner answer; if one was answered, include its follow-up bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every requirement in the epic spec has a corresponding implementation bead.
2. Universal/negative invariants are verified by enumerating every code path that performs the operation, not by citing a single compliant example.
3. Guardrail/scan tests were audited for blind spots, and every spec scenario is pinned by exactly one gate species; no gap candidate proposes tests for a scenario that already has one.
4. Any gaps found are reported as dedupe-ready child-bead candidates under the same epic.
5. If gaps were found, the handoff reports a next-generation reconciliation candidate.
6. The close reason records the reconciliation summary.
Review correction acceptance: Include both module-qualified named tests in pinned invariant inventory (78 mentions/72 unique live attributed declarations), regenerate only evidence inventory/report/artifact-validation and correct PR1354 body. Preserve partial coverage classification, five concrete repair dependencies and gen2. No production/spec/test edits or new tests.

design:
Surface/trust map: own scene/src/timing/{hints,domains,mod}.rs and root exports, plus zero-caller scene helper/field removal and necessary existing-fixture caller edits within scene and its real clients. SceneGraph and BatchTimingHints are runtime mutation authority fed by authenticated protocol boundary; the unused scene TimingHints is a different Rust model, with no producer/persisted serializer. Delete the dead model and DurationUs island only. Preserve live WallUs/MonoUs, test clock, protobuf-to-BatchTimingHints conversion, snapshot/scene mutation consumers, and policy interfaces. Review all 23 groups in dead-code-scene.log against current production callers: leases and limits; font-scale/local-state wrappers; resource/snapshot/tab/tile helpers; zone/widget publishing; unread budget_warning and validation budget constant; timing helpers; node hit IDs; error variants; geometry conversion; action-label limit; widget getters; snapshot/checksum and registry query helpers; is_text_bearing/primary_code. A helper is removable only after resolving app/runtime/protocol/T7 consumers. Where a named invariant needs a zero-production-use constructor/wrapper, use the established scene test-support feature/self-dev-dependency pattern, not a default production API or new feature framework.

Behavior matrix: successful clocked mutations, stale/future/TTL rejections, disconnect/resume/grace, focus/local interaction rendering, lease/policy outcomes and mandatory events retain real authority and ordering. The dead types have no runtime caller, so there is no new concurrency, retry, replay or cleanup algorithm; current session isolation and mutation atomicity remain unchanged. Do not mistake a protobuf TimingHints identifier for a scene user. Error codes, serialization defaults, persisted snapshots and wire representations are unchanged; discovery of a real serialization/caller path means preserve and classify it, not invent a migration. Revert restores deleted internal symbols without data conversion.

Docs impact: remove inaccurate timing/model/export comments in the same diff; current scope/vision/invariant/API semantics remain unchanged, with no new RFC or deferred-framework document. Pre-reset cleanup is separately owned by hud-bstmy.8.3. Inspect app, crates, examples and tests, including the separate tests/integration Cargo package; resolve symbol/type identity and cfg context, not matching comments or names alone. scripts/dead_code.py omits app roots, counts inline test/comment/string identifiers, conflates names, and retains grouped reexports; it is advisory, and successful cargo-check exit does not prove no dead items. For deletion, use compiler/type-lint validation informed by manually checked real callers; preserve contracts with existing behavior tests. Do not add a parallel source-scan, property, snapshot or mirror test species. Public type/field/signature changes require cargo check --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, plus cargo fmt --all --check and repository applicable local gates; never --all-features. Use CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 on this host and repository just/llvmpipe recipes for GPU checks. Reconcile the complete current invariant-name inventory (72 names at baseline), not just a sampled subset.

Nearest behavior gates: retain all currently named scene/policy/resource/protocol invariants, especially tile TTL, timing stale/future boundaries, policy/budget, ownership, and grpc disconnect/resume/grace tests. The existing 16 dead hints tests and 4 DurationUs tests are removed with the island (Tests: +0 ~0 -20); no replacement mapper/timing mirror suite. Further narrowing may alter existing fixtures only, with a precise final delta. Cohesion: S is an independently reversible scene-internal deletion outcome. It shares protocol fixture/gate context with P/T, so run in the coordinator serial lane order, not concurrent overlapping public type edits.

title: T8.1a: Dead code in protocol, resource and scene
description:
Delete production code with no production caller in tze_hud_protocol, tze_hud_resource and tze_hud_scene (zero-decision deletions found by reference counts plus the narrow-to-pub(crate) rustc check).

Line refs are at windows-release-pipeline@44d355ef (same content as main@1eb8f7cb); re-grep symbols before editing. The planning survey is not persisted; this bead is self-contained.
design: Method per crate: narrow pub items to pub(crate) (keep pub on names other crates' non-test code use), `cargo check -p C --lib`, delete what rustc flags as dead_code, then re-check. Text matching is a lower bound.
